files.name: principle-laziness-protocol
files.description: Apply when refactoring or tempted to add an abstraction, layer, wrapper, or signal threading. Signals: "should I generalize this?", a growing diff, new config or indirection, speculative flexibility, evaluating diff size.

files.name: principle-foundational-thinking
files.description: Apply before writing logic, when choosing core types and data structures, ordering scaffold vs features, or deciding what concurrent actors share. Signals: "where do I start", defining the model, picking a representation, planning a build.

files.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
files.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Signals: "just add a flag or case here", bolting a feature onto the current structure, special-casing a model that was designed without it.

files.name: principle-attack-the-premise
files.description: Apply when two or more fixes that assumed the same thing have failed the same gate again. Signals: repeated "my fix didn't work", same test or error returning, several patches sharing one hidden assumption.

files.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
files.description: Apply when about to add code, a validator, a parser, or a feature to an existing system. Signals: reaching to build first, dead code still present, speculative guards or templates, before laying new scaffold.

files.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
files.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Signals: "where does this come from?", stacked one-caller wrappers or adapters, pass-through layers, hidden or widely mutable state, hard-to-follow control flow.

files.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
files.description: Apply during a planned rewrite or migration with explicit phase boundaries. Signals: "keep everything green at every step", throwaway compatibility code, phased rewrite toward a target architecture, intermediate breakage decisions.

files.name: principle-experience-first
files.description: Apply when making product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Signals: "ship more features vs polish these", adding options or controls, cutting scope, choosing implementation convenience over user delight.

files.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
files.description: Apply when facing a UI interaction or architecture choice with no precedent in the codebase, or one whose quality depends on feel. Signals: "how should this work?", novel component, no existing pattern to copy, picking between approaches.

files.name: principle-build-the-lever
files.description: Apply before doing a non-trivial edit, migration, batch analysis, or check by hand. Signals: "let me just fix these one by one", many similar edits, a sweep or migration, a verification you'll rerun.

files.name: principle-model-the-domain
files.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats the same shape assumption across files. Signals: a growing if/else chain, a second boolean that must stay in sync, scattered lifecycle checks, load-validate-transform-save modules.

files.name: principle-boundary-discipline
files.description: Apply when wiring up validation, error handling, or adapting to a CLI, config, network, or framework. Signals: duplicate nil or empty checks deep in call chains, parsing args or config, defensive code everywhere, wire types leaking inward.

files.name: principle-type-system-discipline
files.description: Apply when designing types or reviewing a function signature in a statically-typed language. Signals: stringly-typed ids, interchangeable primitives of different meaning, untyped JSON or rows crossing in, any or casts, handling enum and variant cases.

files.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
files.description: Apply when designing a command, lifecycle step, or processing loop that can crash, restart, or retry. Signals: re-running a job, leftover lock, temp, or half-written state, "what if it runs twice", retries, resume.

files.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
files.description: Apply when a new internal API exists but old callers remain and no external users need backward compat. Signals: leaving a shim or compat layer "for now", an old function still referenced after a refactor, breaking-change cleanup.

files.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
files.description: Apply when concurrent actors or subagents might write the same file, branch, key, or state object. Signals: race conditions, two workers editing one state.json, "we need a lock", parallel writes to a shared target.

files.name: principle-prove-it-works
files.description: Apply after finishing a task, before declaring it done. Signals: "it compiles", tests pass, an agent's self-report, "should work now", about to mark complete or open a PR.

files.name: principle-fix-root-causes
files.description: Apply when debugging and about to patch where the symptom appeared. Signals: stack trace, adding a guard, retry, or try-catch at the failure line, "just handle this case", error surfacing far from its source.

files.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
files.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, batches of similar edits) and when ordering commits or PRs. Signals: "let me do them all then test", a long run of changes, stacking commits, batching verification to the end.

files.name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
files.description: Apply when writing, changing, or keeping a test. Signals: mocking internal helpers, asserting call order or which collaborator ran, tests that break on every refactor, snapshotting the implementation.

files.name: principle-explain-the-number
files.description: Apply before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured. Signals: speedup, regression, throughput, latency, benchmark result, eval score, "it's 2x faster", "the test got slower".

files.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
files.description: Apply when context is filling up on a long run. Signals: large outputs, reading big or long files repeatedly, fan-out planning, "context almost full", compression kicking in.

files.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
files.description: Apply when about to ask "should I do X?" on reversible work. Signals: pausing for confirmation mid-task, "do you want me to proceed?", asking permission for an edit you can undo.

files.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
files.description: Apply when you notice yourself writing the same instruction or correction a second time, or the same mistake keeps coming back. Signals: repeating guidance in prompts or docs, "I keep telling it to...", recurring review comments.
